EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Strait of Hormuz has become a critical flashpoint after Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship, causing damage but no casualties, following warnings regarding unauthorized transit routes. Concurrently, Iran has proposed charging transit fees in the Strait, a move vehemently rejected by the United States and Gulf states, amplifying maritime security concerns in a vital global chokepoint. Despite international pressure, Israel maintains its military presence in "security zones" across Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza, while suffering a combat fatality and injuries in Lebanon and continuing strikes against Hezbollah and Palestinian Islamic Jihad.

IRAN
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship, the "Ever Lovely," near the coast of Oman, close to the Strait of Hormuz, causing damage to the ship's bridge but no casualties. This incident occurred hours after the IRGC issued warnings to ships against using routes not approved by the Iranian regime. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) stated that any passage outside its designated framework would not be covered by safe passage guarantees or insurance, and consequences would fall on the vessel's owner/operator. Iran has proposed a plan to collect an estimated $40 billion annually in "security, safety, and environmental services" fees from ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, intending to share revenue with neighboring Gulf states. This proposal has been met with firm opposition from the US, Oman, and other Gulf states, who insist on free international waterways. Several vessels, including two oil supertankers, reportedly changed course to avoid an Omani parallel route in the Strait.

Diplomatically, Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, denied US claims that unfrozen Iranian assets would be used to purchase American agricultural products, stating Iran would procure necessities based on competitive criteria from any suitable global source. Qalibaf also stated that a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon is a "red line" and a condition for a final agreement between Iran and the US. Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani warned Israel to "leave all of Lebanon" voluntarily, or face "humiliation and defeat," referencing the 2000 withdrawal from Bint Jbeil. The Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed ongoing dialogue with Oman regarding the "framework for future administration and maritime services in the Strait of Hormuz," focusing on temporary arrangements for a 60-day period. Russia expressed readiness to participate in a UN Security Council resolution for a final US-Iran agreement. An unofficial Telegram account linked to the IRGC claimed Yahya Hosseini Panjaki, commander of the "Handaleh" hacker unit, was killed in an attack during the recent conflict, though this remains unconfirmed by official sources. Iranian President Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Araghchi expressed condolences and offered aid to Venezuela following its recent earthquakes.

ISRAEL
Israel continued military operations in Lebanon and Gaza. In southern Lebanon, the IDF reported killing at least six Hezbollah operatives in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and the Ali Taher ridge area who posed a threat to ground forces. Troops from the Golani Brigade and Commando Brigade were involved, utilizing Israeli Air Force strikes and ground fire. A Master Sgt. (res.) Basil Sweid, 32, from Peki'in, a truck driver in the 7th Armored Brigade's 75th Battalion, was killed in an "operational accident" when his refueling truck overturned in the Rab al-Thalathine area of southern Lebanon. Another soldier was moderately injured in the same incident. An IDF soldier was also moderately injured in a separate "operational accident" in southern Lebanon.

In Gaza, the IDF announced the killing of Adam Muhammad Ibrahim Abu Hadid, a commander in Palestinian Islamic Jihad's (PIJ) "weapon production array," in a strike in Khan Younis earlier this week. The IDF stated he was involved in manufacturing and supplying weapons and posed an immediate threat. Defense Minister Israel Katz affirmed that Israeli forces would remain indefinitely in "security zones" in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza to protect residents from "jihadist elements." Prime Minister Netanyahu echoed this, stating, "We will remain as long as required in the security zone in southern Lebanon," and reiterated that Iran would "never have nuclear weapons" under his premiership. Netanyahu also acknowledged calls of "Go home" during an IDF cadets graduation ceremony, alongside counter-chants of support.

On the home front, President Isaac Herzog's helicopter made an emergency landing at Palmachim Airbase after a bird strike, causing no injuries. Two teenagers, aged 15 and 17, were shot in Jaffa, with one 17-year-old later pronounced dead; the motive is suspected to be criminal. The Attorney General supports denying tax benefits to religious institutions where draft dodgers study. The Association of Hesder Yeshivas announced that students would enlist in the Armored Corps in August following discussions with the IDF Chief of Staff. Head of Planning and Manpower Directorate Brig. Gen. Shai Tayeb stated the IDF needs to extend mandatory service to 36 months to meet military needs.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces continued operations in the Gaza Strip, including the targeted killing of a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) commander, Adam Muhammad Ibrahim Abu Hadid, in Khan Younis earlier this week. Israeli President Herzog stated that the IDF controls "around 60% of the Gaza Strip" following the October 7 attack and subsequent war, calling for the implementation of President Trump's "21-point plan," primarily the disarmament of Hamas. Hamas issued a statement accusing Israel of continuing a policy of "genocide" in Gaza through blockade, starvation, and targeting children and civilians. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli occupation authorities expropriated 115 acres of Palestinian land for illegal settlement expansion by designating it as "state land."

LEBANON
Israeli military operations targeted Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon. The IDF confirmed killing at least six Hezbollah members, five in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and one armed operative in the Ali Taher ridge area. These individuals were deemed threats to Israeli forces. The IDF also reported an "operational accident" in Rab al-Thalathine, southern Lebanon, resulting in the death of Master Sgt. (res.) Basil Sweid, 32, a truck driver, and the moderate injury of another soldier when a refueling truck overturned. Another IDF soldier was moderately injured in a separate incident.

Reports from Reuters, citing a senior US official, claimed Israel had withdrawn from parts of its "security zone" in southern Lebanon, with the Lebanese army expected to deploy in its place. However, these claims were denied by both Israeli security and military officials, who stated no withdrawal instructions had been received, and by a Lebanese military source to Al Jazeera, who stated no Israeli forces withdrawal had been documented. Israeli Defense Minister Katz and Prime Minister Netanyahu reiterated that Israel would remain in security zones in Lebanon "without any time limit."
Hezbollah MP Sheikh Naim Qassem warned the Lebanese government against making any concessions to Israel, stating no agreement would be implemented without Hezbollah's understanding and a complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory. Italy and France announced a new coalition to support Lebanon once the UNIFIL mandate expires at year's end, signaling plans for a potential international conference. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also mentioned that "results yesterday of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel were very good," suggesting ongoing discussions, though specifics remain undisclosed.

SYRIA & IRAQ
No direct military operations by Israel in Syria were explicitly reported in the provided messages, though Israeli Defense Minister Katz stated Israeli forces would remain in "security zones" in Syria indefinitely.

In Iraq, an explosion occurred at an ammunition depot belonging to the Popular Mobilization Units (PMU) within the Mansouriya camp in Diyala province, according to the Iraqi Ministry of Defense. Initial reports indicated no casualties. However, the 24th Brigade of the PMU denied any incident at their Mansouriya camp, leading to conflicting reports. Iraq's Ministry of Oil issued a statement clarifying that earlier reports about Iraq considering leaving OPEC were not official government positions, but rather internal discussions. Iraq affirmed its commitment to OPEC, emphasizing the need for its production quotas to be reassessed and significantly increased due to a severe financial crisis exacerbated by regional conflicts impacting oil exports. The Iraqi cabinet reportedly decided to halt new investment contracts and advised companies with existing contracts to "be patient," possibly due to the financial strains. Unconfirmed reports from Lebanese and Syrian local sources mentioned a gathering of "Joulani forces" on the Lebanese border. Iraqi border guards thwarted an attempt to smuggle 34 kg of drugs via an air balloon on the Iraq-Jordan-Syria border. A military intelligence officer was killed in Baghdad following armed clashes in the Ma'alef area.

GULF STATES
The Gulf States, particularly in conjunction with the United States, have expressed strong opposition to Iran's proposed transit fees for the Strait of Hormuz. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, following a meeting with Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, reiterated President Trump's stance that "no costs for passage through the Strait of Hormuz will exist," and stated there is "no support from Gulf countries for imposing fees or taxes." Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi also publicly stated that future arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz "will not include transit tolls."

A joint US-GCC statement welcomed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Washington and Tehran, acknowledging mediation efforts by Pakistan and Qatar. However, it also underscored the necessity of addressing Iranian threats, including missiles, drones, and support for proxies, to achieve regional peace. The statement emphasized the critical importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ensuring unrestricted freedom of navigation for regional and global security. It also conditioned any investment or trade with Iran on its adherence to the MoU and a final agreement. Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan held discussions with both US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi regarding the Iran-US understanding and regional security.

Iraq is reportedly considering leaving OPEC if its oil production quota is not substantially increased, citing a severe financial crisis due to conflict-related disruptions to oil exports. This internal discussion, reported by Reuters, highlights economic pressures on Gulf states stemming from regional instability.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **IRGC Attack in Strait of Hormuz:** Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps attacked the Singapore-flagged cargo ship "Ever Lovely" near Oman's coast (near Strait of Hormuz), causing damage but no casualties, following Iranian warnings about unauthorized routes.
2.  **Iran's Proposed Hormuz Fees:** Iran proposed an annual $40 billion in "security, safety, and environmental services" fees for Strait of Hormuz transit, seeking revenue sharing with Gulf states; this was rejected by the US and Oman.
3.  **Israeli Withdrawal from Lebanon Denied:** Reports from Reuters of an Israeli withdrawal from parts of southern Lebanon were denied by the IDF and Lebanese military sources, while Israeli officials stated forces would remain indefinitely in "security zones."
4.  **Hezbollah Operatives Killed:** The IDF reported killing at least six Hezbollah operatives in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Ali Taher ridge area in southern Lebanon, who posed threats to Israeli ground forces.
5.  **Israeli Soldier Killed in Lebanon:** Master Sgt. (res.) Basil Sweid, 32, was killed, and another soldier moderately injured, in an "operational accident" involving an overturned refueling truck in Rab al-Thalathine, southern Lebanon.
6.  **PIJ Commander Killed in Gaza:** The IDF killed Adam Muhammad Ibrahim Abu Hadid, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander in charge of weapon production, in a strike in Khan Younis, Gaza.
7.  **US-Iran Direct Military Channel:** US Vice President J.D. Vance stated that an initial agreement was reached to establish a direct military communication channel between the IRGC and CENTCOM in Doha to de-escalate disputes.
8.  **Iraq's OPEC Membership Under Review:** Iraq is internally discussing a potential exit from OPEC if its oil production quota is not significantly increased, citing a severe financial crisis exacerbated by regional conflicts.
9.  **Venezuela Earthquake Disaster:** Two severe earthquakes (M7.2 and M7.5) struck Venezuela, with reported casualties rising to at least 164-188 dead and 1,520 injured; early reports of 50,000 missing are unverified.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
**Escalation Risks in Strait of Hormuz:** The IRGC's attack on a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel and Iran's proposal for transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz pose a significant risk of escalation. This action directly challenges international maritime law and could lead to confrontation if Iran attempts to enforce its fee system or restrict passage, as implied by the PGSA statements. The US and Gulf states' firm rejection of these fees highlights a red line.
**Lebanon Front Volatility:** The sustained Israeli military presence in southern Lebanon, combined with continued strikes against Hezbollah and the death of an Israeli soldier in an operational accident, keeps this front highly volatile. Hezbollah's and Iran's insistence on a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon as a "red line" for any diplomatic agreement creates a fundamental disagreement that could easily spark wider conflict. The IDF's continued operations in Hezbollah's underground complex at Ali Taher ridge are a particular flashpoint.
**Regional Proxy Confrontation:** Israeli Defense Minister Katz's pledge to remain in "security zones" in Syria and Gaza, coupled with the ongoing targeted killing of PIJ commanders, indicates a continued proactive stance against "jihadist elements." Iran's support for proxies like Hezbollah and the Houthis, as highlighted by US Secretary of State Rubio, remains a source of regional instability and a potential trigger for broader conflict.
**Military Posture Changes:** The IDF's internal discussions about extending mandatory military service to 36 months, alongside its current operational tempo in multiple arenas, suggest a long-term commitment to its current security strategy. Iran's Quds Force commander's direct threats against Israel underscore a continued readiness for confrontation, particularly in Lebanon. The US's push for a direct military communication channel with Iran, if implemented, could potentially de-escalate future incidents but does not negate underlying tensions.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:**
*   **Strait of Hormuz:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio firmly rejected Iran's proposed transit fees, stating "no costs for passage through the Strait of Hormuz will exist" and that the US has not transferred any funds to Iran. He reiterated that "no country in the world supports paying for passage through straits."
*   **Iran Diplomacy:** Rubio welcomed the Iran-US MoU but cautioned that the deal would not work if Iran used funds to support proxies and missile programs. Vice President J.D. Vance claimed an initial agreement for a direct military communication channel between an IRGC official and CENTCOM in Doha to resolve disputes. President Trump acknowledged Senate's vote on War Powers Act regarding Iran, but it failed to advance. He also claimed China and Russia stayed out of the "war in Iran" because he asked them to.
*   **Venezuela:** The US, through Trump and Rubio, offered "big, fast, effective" support and mobilized SOUTHCOM for a "whole-of-government" relief effort after the earthquakes.
**Gulf States:**
*   **Strait of Hormuz:** Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi publicly rejected transit tolls for the Strait. A joint US-GCC statement welcomed the Iran-US MoU but condemned Iranian-backed attacks by proxies in Iraq and emphasized open navigation in Hormuz, conditioning future trade with Iran on adherence to the MoU. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister discussed these developments with both Rubio and Busaidi.
*   **Iraq:** Iraq's Ministry of Oil clarified that internal discussions about leaving OPEC due to financial crisis are not an official government position, but it seeks a significant increase in its oil production quota.
**Europe:**
*   **Lebanon:** Italy's PM Meloni and France's President Macron announced a new coalition to support Lebanon after the UNIFIL mandate expires and discussed a potential international conference. Italy's PM Meloni and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani denied NATO Secretary General's claims of Italian bases being used for US attacks on Iran, stating no such use occurred or would occur.
*   **Russia:** Russia's Foreign Ministry expressed readiness to participate in drafting a UN Security Council resolution for a final Iran-US agreement. France intercepted a Russian-linked "shadow fleet" tanker near Sicily.
**Turkey:**
*   Israel's Foreign Minister Saar will bring a proposal to the government to formally recognize the Armenian Genocide, seen as a retaliatory measure against Turkey's Erdogan. Trump claimed he asked Erdogan to stay out of the "war with Iran," which he did, and suggested re-evaluating F-35 sales to Turkey.
**United Nations:** UN agencies are mobilizing aid for Venezuela following the devastating earthquakes. The International Maritime Organization temporarily suspended its plan to evacuate ships from the Strait of Hormuz after the attack on the cargo vessel.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
1.  **Strait of Hormuz Ship Naming Discrepancy:** One source (Faytuks Network) refers to the attacked ship as "Ever Lovely" and then immediately as "Ever Lonely." Other sources (N12, Asafroz, Shargh) use more general terms like "Singapore-flagged cargo ship." This suggests a potential typo or initial confusion regarding the specific vessel's name.
2.  **Conflicting Reports on Israeli Withdrawal from Lebanon:** There are direct contradictions regarding an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon. A senior American official told Reuters that Israel had withdrawn from parts of its security zone, with the Lebanese army expected to deploy there. However, Israeli security and military officials, as well as a Lebanese military source (Al Jazeera), explicitly denied any such withdrawal, stating no instructions had been given. This may indicate a diplomatic overture being misinterpreted as a military action, a trial balloon, or deliberate misinformation.
3.  **Unverified Death of Iranian Hacker Commander:** The reported death of Yahya Hosseini Panjaki, commander of the "Handaleh" hacker unit, in an Israeli targeted killing during the "last war in Iran" is attributed to an "unofficial Telegram account linked to the IRGC" and a "Telegram channel identified with the IRGC intelligence organization." This lacks official confirmation and should be treated with caution, potentially a propaganda claim or an unconfirmed leak.
4.  **Exaggerated Venezuela Casualty Figures:** Initial crowdsourced data cited by Faytuks Network claimed "over 50,000 people are reported missing" in Venezuela after the earthquake, noting it's "unofficial reports from extended family unable to reach relatives, and it’s likely many are due to lost cell/internet coverage." This number is significantly higher than official Venezuelan government figures (164-188 dead, 1,520 injured, ~200 trapped) and US geological survey estimates (10,000-100,000 dead, a broad range). The 50,000 figure is likely a severe overestimation due to communication breakdown and should be viewed with skepticism.
5.  **Propaganda and Rhetoric regarding Iran-US Agreement:** There is a clear "war of narratives" between Washington and Tehran regarding the nature and implications of their ongoing negotiations. US officials (Trump, Vance) claim Iranian assets will be used for American agricultural products and a direct military channel is agreed, while Iranian officials (Qalibaf) vehemently deny these claims, accusing the US of "false claims" and "decades of mistrust." This suggests an effort by both sides to shape public perception and exert leverage.
6.  **Iraqi PMU Explosion Discrepancies:** The Iraqi Ministry of Defense reported an explosion at an ammunition depot of the PMU in Diyala with no casualties. However, the 24th Brigade of the PMU explicitly denied any incident at their camp, stating all operations were normal and secure. This contradiction raises questions about the transparency of reporting from Iraqi security forces regarding internal incidents.
7.  **Iranian "War" with Israel:** Several Iranian sources, including Press TV and Quds Force commander Qaani, refer to a recent "war against Iran" or "US-Israeli imposed war on Iran." Details on specific military engagements directly involving Iran and Israel are limited in this intelligence feed, beyond the Hormuz incident and Israeli claims of preventing Iranian nuclear weapons. This suggests a broader framing of the regional conflict by Iranian sources, which may encompass proxy engagements or less publicized direct actions.
